sourceReview.finding: Origin releases each returned block through finally, including write failure and truncation hold. It computes only the final flushed-block digest before dropping that block, preserving the original prefixSha256 meaning. The input stream closes and its reference is cleared before active interval decrement and terminal logging.

Gateway clears each normal or IncompleteRead.partial block before another read and before terminal bookkeeping, while preserving failed transport state, returned-byte counters and firstBodyChunkAt location. Existing response/connection close remains before final activity/log bookkeeping.

Collector clears response blocks on every iteration and exceptional exit, closes its response before settling control observations and clears comparison chunks before metadata. The original one-byte initial read and firstBodyByte clock remain at the same semantic point; failures still remain failures.

export_body_observation confines actual/expected Slice bodies to one helper invocation, returns only byte count/hash/equality metadata and clears them on success or exception. Existing read_export_body size checks are retained. Reassembly writes/hashes/counts identical bytes and releases each block through finally; it does not trim an invalid export or turn a mismatch into success.

Eleven targeted methods exercise weak-referenceable synthetic payloads across Origin normal/truncate/write-error, Gateway normal/incomplete/write-error, adjacent exports and source/output failure, and Collector response/comparison/control/metadata boundaries. Assertions retain digest, result and first-body timing semantics. Existing tests were not edited; the lifetime test module is new.
